Subject: DPIA evidence & identity provisioning: next steps

Hi Thomas —

Thanks again for the call this morning. To keep momentum on the DPIA and audit-readiness requests, attached is a compact evidence inventory and an access matrix template that we can populate collaboratively. Quick asks from our side so we can scope the work: 

- Can you confirm the list of roles that need remote read-only console access (e.g., InfoSec reviewers, privacy team)?
- Do you prefer a SAML test IdP for verification, or should we issue time-limited service accounts?
- Are you requesting a point-in-time export of Article 30 processing records, or continuous exports for a specified window?

We can provide: an Article 30 CSV export, an exported subprocessor roster, sample KMS key rotation logs, and a short walkthrough of our console read-only view (no data extraction by default). See attachments: evidence_inventory.csv, access-matrix-template.xlsx.

Proposed timeline: once you confirm roles and preferred access method we can:
- Day 0–1: share export and pre-filled access matrix
- Day 2–3: conduct a short remote session to validate console/read-only access
- Day 4: hand over final artifacts and a short summary memo for the DPIA record

Looping in Marissa (security ops) to help schedule the remote validation.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Ben —

Appreciate the clear rundown and the attachments. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Roles: our InfoSec reviewer (me), Privacy lead (Kaitlyn), and a compliance auditor (third party) will need read-only access. We will provide email addresses once we confirm the compliance auditor.
- Identity provisioning: we prefer a SAML test IdP so we can validate SSO integration without creating persistent service accounts. Can Redwood provide a short SAML metadata file and a test SP endpoint?
- Art.30 export: a point-in-time export covering July–Aug 2027 should be sufficient for our DPIA right now. If we need a longer window we'll ask.

Also: can you confirm whether your access logs include agent IPs and exact API call names (for sampling)? That will be useful for our audit trail.

Thanks — putting this into our internal ticket.

Thomas Reed

- We can provide SAML metadata and a test SP endpoint within 48 hours. Marissa will coordinate a short SSO validation window (30–60 minutes).
- For the compliance auditor we will issue a read-only console role scoped to the DPIA folder; access will be time-limited and logged.

2) Evidence exports
- Attached: art30_export_20270914.csv (point-in-time export for Jul–Aug 2027). This includes processing activity entries, subprocessors, and legal basis mapping.
- Access logs: we can provide sample call-level logs including timestamps, API endpoint names, and agent IPs (redacted for internal security per our policy). If Oceans Bank needs full IPs for the audit, specify the legal basis and we'll evaluate per our DPA and lawful disclosure process.

3) Audit session
- Suggest scheduling the remote validation session for Mon/Tue next week (we'll propose slots). We'll use screen-sharing and SAML test accounts; no live data extraction will be performed.

Lauren — can you review the access duration proposed (48 hours for auditor access) and confirm it's within the standard enterprise temporary access policy?

Thanks,
